questions.question: The postorder traversal of a binary tree is 8,9,6,7,4,5,2,3,1. The inorder traversal of the same tree is 8,6,9,4,7,2,5,1,3. The height of a tree is the length of the longest path from the root to any leaf. The height of the binary tree above is ______.
questions.explanation:
Postorder ends with 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] root 1. Inorder splits into left {8, 6, 9, 4, 7, 2, 5} and right {3}.
- Left subtree: root 2 (last in its postorder), with left {8, 6, 9, 4, 7} and right {5}.
- {8, 6, 9, 4, 7}: root 4, left {8, 6, 9} (root 6 with children 8, 9), right {7}.

Longest path: 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 = 4 edges.

Answer: 4

questions.question:
Let SLLdel be a function that deletes a node in a singly-linked list given a pointer to the node and a pointer to the head of the list. Similarly, let DLLdel be another function that deletes a node in a doubly-linked list given a pointer to the node and a pointer to the head of the list.
Let n denote the number of nodes in each of the linked lists. Which one of the following choices is TRUE about the worst-case time complexity of SLLdel and DLLdel?

options.A: SLLdel is O(1) and DLLdel is O(n)
options.B: Both SLLdel and DLLdel are O(log(n))
options.C: Both SLLdel and DLLdel are O(1)
options.D: SLLdel is O(n) and DLLdel is O(1)

questions.explanation:
To delete a node we must update its predecessor's next pointer.

- Singly linked list: the predecessor is found only by walking from the head [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(n)[/latex].
- Doubly linked list: the node's prev pointer gives the predecessor directly [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: SLLdel is O(n) and DLLdel is O(1)

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.question:
Consider the following pseudo code, where x and y are positive integers. 
 begin
   q := 0
    r := x 
    while r >= y  do
         begin
               r := r - y
              q := q + 1
        end
end
The post condition that needs to be satisfied after the program terminates is
questions.explanation:
The loop subtracts y from r and counts it in q, which is division of x by y. Invariant: x = qy + r. The loop stops when r [latex]\lt[/latex] y.

Answer: {x = qy + r [latex]\wedge[/latex] r [latex]\lt[/latex] y}

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.question:
The attributes of three arithmetic operators in some programming language are given below.

The value of the expression 2-5+1-7*3 in this language is_______ .
questions.explanation:
Precedence: + (highest) [latex]\gt[/latex] [latex]-[/latex] [latex]\gt[/latex] * (lowest). So * is applied last:
[latex](2-5+1-7)*3[/latex]

Inside: + first, 5 + 1 = 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]-[/latex] 6 [latex]-[/latex] 7. [latex]-[/latex] is right associative: [latex]2-(6-7)=2-(-1)=3[/latex].

[latex]3*3=9[/latex]

Answer: 9

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Let F(x, y) = foo(x, y, 10). Both values go 15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]-[/latex]5.
- F([latex]-[/latex]5, [latex]-[/latex]5) = 10
- F(5, [latex]-[/latex]5) = F([latex]-[/latex]5, [latex]-[/latex]5) = 10, and similarly F([latex]-[/latex]5, 5) = 10
- F(5, 5) = F(5, [latex]-[/latex]5) + F([latex]-[/latex]5, 5) = 20
- F(15, [latex]-[/latex]5) = F(5, [latex]-[/latex]5) = 10, so F(15, 5) = F(15, [latex]-[/latex]5) + F(5, 5) = 30
- By symmetry F(5, 15) = 30

F(15, 15) = F(15, 5) + F(5, 15) = 60

Answer: 60

questions.question: Consider a binary min-heap containing 105 distinct elements. Let [latex]k[/latex]  be the index (in the underlying array) of the maximum element stored in the heap. The number of possible values of [latex]k[/latex] is
questions.explanation:
In a min-heap every parent is smaller than its children, so the maximum element cannot have a child [latex]\text{---}[/latex] it must be a leaf. Any leaf can hold it.

In an array heap of [latex]n[/latex] elements, leaves are at indices [latex]\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1[/latex] to [latex]n[/latex].

[latex]n=105[/latex]: leaves are 53 to 105 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]105-52=53[/latex] positions.

Answer: 53

questions.question:
Let S1 and S2 be two stacks. S1 has capacity of 4 elements. S2 has capacity of 2 elements. S1 already has 4 elements: 100, 200, 300, and 400, whereas S2 is empty, as shown below.

[latex] \begin{array}{|c|} \hline 400 (Top) \\ \hline 300 \\ \hline 200\\ \hline 100 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
Stack S1

[latex] \begin{array}{|c|} \hline \\ \hline \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
Stack S2

Only the following three operations are available:

PushToS2: Pop the top element from S1 and push it on S2.
PushToS1: Pop the top element from S2 and push it on S1.
GenerateOutput: Pop the top element from S1 and output it to the user.

Note that the pop operation is not allowed on an empty stack and the push operation is not allowed on a full stack.

Which of the following output sequences can be generated by using the above operations?
questions.explanation:
S1 = 100, 200, 300, 400 (top). S2 can hold only 2 elements.

- 100, 200, 400, 300: to output 100 first, 400, 300, 200 (3 elements) must go to S2 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] impossible.
- 200, 300, 400, 100: move 400, 300 to S2; output 200; move 300 back, output 300; move 400 back, output 400; output 100 True
- 400, 200, 100, 300: output 400; move 300 to S2; output 200, 100; move 300 back, output 300 True
- 300, 200, 400, 100: move 400 to S2; output 300, 200; move 400 back, output 400; output 100 True

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4
